title: Foulkes' conjecture for the sixth symmetric power
main_claim: For every b>=6 and every finite-dimensional complex V there is a GL(V)-equivariant injection Sym^6(Sym^b V) -> Sym^b(Sym^6 V), i.e. h_b[h_6]-h_6[h_b] is Schur-positive.
coverage: Read all sections: reduction, upper, lower, certificates, band, verification. Checked by hand: the Cauchy-decomposition formula for F and the det^6 shift F(d+6e_6)=F(d); the rectangle occurrence and the highest-weight multiplication monotonicity; the chart lemma (factor counting through Newton, polarization and inclusion-exclusion) and the first-row corollary (Y-degree of f/z^b is lambda_2+...+lambda_6, at most b); the polarization lemma (sl2 injectivity of D_i^L needs weight j-(i-1)L >= L, i.e. j >= aL) and Prop. large (L=(a-1)^2, so b>=150 at a=6); the signed-strip determinant lemma and its interlacing bounds; the chain-count bound U and its monotonicity; the target and source Newton recurrences, including the strip enumeration with fixed least residues; the sumset triangulation bound and the power certificate. I checked the monotonicity of f(C,h,k) in h symbolically with python over a grid. In the band section I checked the alternant extraction with x=(1,q,y), the Gaussian-polynomial target expansion with its b-k=-1 boundary, the binary-complement source formula (only t=b+1 is extra, since t<=27<=b+1), the G_j sign and q^j bookkeeping, the Euler recurrence, the cross-factor coefficients, the A=y^{-rho}a_rho alternation, and the Laurent support window [-162,157] with the D^{-1} division range. Mode/residue transport logic in the certificates section is consistent with Lemma rectangles and Prop. upper. Ran verify_computations.py --check: PASS. I could not run the full C++ computations because Boost is not installed.

issues.location: Sections 5-6, Verifications 5.x and 6.x (finite certificates and band)
issues.description: The finite part of the proof (b from 6 to 25 directly, then flagged pairs and band nonnegativity for b from 26 to 29, or up to 149 on the independent route) rests entirely on executing two C++ programs. The formulas these programs implement are correctly derived, but I did not re-execute them in this audit.
issues.evidence: Only the --check mode (hashes, tables, numeric bounds) was run, and it passed. The --run mode needs Boost headers, which are absent here.

issues.description: The main route for b>=30 uses Theorem 1 of the companion paper OpenAIQuadratic2026 (surjectivity for b>=a(a-1)), which I did not audit. The paper also supplies a complete independent route: Prop. large (b>=150) plus the finite checks through b=149. I checked that route and found it sound, so the main theorem does not depend on the companion.
issues.evidence: Remark at the end of Section 7 and Prop. prop:large: L=(a-1)^2, b>=a(a-1)^2=150.

sibling_notes: No sibling entries in fam:210 at audit time. If another branch audits OpenAIQuadratic2026 (surjectivity of the Chow multiplication map for b>=a(a-1)), its result only affects the shorter route here. The independent chart+polarization route (b>=a(a-1)^2) checks out.
